evidence: RFC-0001 through RFC-0006 define scope, pipeline, objects, resolution, review, and benchmarking.
conformance/requirements.json maps all 200 normative source units.
RFC dependency validation reports no unknown dependency or cycle.
Conformance extraction reports no unmapped or stale normative source unit.
Registry validation enforces unique active IDs, paths, dependencies, and frontmatter alignment.
GOVERNANCE.md and COMPATIBILITY.md prohibit silent ID reuse in 1.x.
All 60 registered runtime objects are active and resolve through the generated index.
The starter config pins specification 1.0.0 and the generated registry source revision.
Human-signals and editor guidance preserves supplied voice, source boundaries, and finding-driven revisions under the unchanged normative profile.
The offline reference runner, workflow, source snapshots, adapters, and guarded transitions pass the unit suite.
Compatibility documentation does not present reference tooling as a fully conforming universal writing engine.
CLI version and help are checked against the installed package version from an unrelated working directory without Python on PATH.
Twenty-one reviewed examples cover all 11 registered topics and all 11 platform families.
High-risk examples preserve their non-advisory editorial-method boundary.
Six new RU/EN editing exercises are explicitly informative and are not counted as full reviewed examples or comparative quality evidence.
Two benchmark cases retain controlled arms and evaluator separation.
Three visual fixtures preserve auto-none, selected-asset, and hard-failure handling.
README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG, SECURITY, SUPPORT, GOVERNANCE, compatibility, migration, and release documentation are present.
Manifest-defined release verification is offline and CI-reproducible.

external_review.notes: No independent external normative review is claimed for 1.1.1; public review remains welcome and will inform compatible 1.x clarifications or a future major revision.

limitations: This review was performed inside the project workflow and is not independent.
Implementation requirements remain planned unless a concrete engine supplies the declared verification evidence.
No public comparative model-quality benchmark result is part of the 1.1.1 release claim.
